A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the teacher-student model is a useful tool for the analysis of realistic learning problems, provided that the feature maps are generic enough.

the Gaussian covariate teacher-student model provides a simple and powerful framework to describe the learning curves of realistic datasets, and that this is possible with a very simple model that is not trained on the target dataset, but only on the covariates.

the teacher-student model can be used to describe the learning curve of a large number of realistic supervised learning problems, provided that the teacher and student act on the right feature spaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, under a broad set of conditions, the teacher-student model is capable of capturing the learning behaviour of a broad range of feature maps.

, despite its apparent simplicity, the teacher-student model can provide an insightful description of the behaviour of realistic learning problems, and that this behaviour is strongly related to the choice of the feature map.
the teacher-student model can be seen as a generic tool to understand the behaviour of supervised learning algorithms in high dimensions.
